# Anthropic - Manager of Applied AI Architecture, Partnerships briefing packet
| Manager of Applied AI Architecture, Partnerships | $315,000–$380,000 USD | Reports to Partnerships (GTM context) |

## JD Complement
This is a scale-design role at the intersection of enterprise AI, external delivery capacity, and technical trust. Anthropic needs partners to help customers move from interest in frontier models to durable, governed use in real workflows.

The core tension is expansion without erosion: broaden enterprise reach through an ecosystem while preserving the quality, safety posture, and architectural consistency associated with Anthropic.

A strong leader in this seat would turn complex field learning into repeatable methods, helping partners deliver credible outcomes without requiring Anthropic specialists to remain embedded in every implementation.

## Company DNA & Operating Model
Anthropic is a public benefit corporation founded in 2021 and headquartered in San Francisco. Claude is its principal product family, supported by an identity centered on AI systems that are reliable, interpretable, and steerable.

The company combines frontier-model research with an increasingly broad enterprise product surface. Claude serves business users, developers, and organizations building AI-enabled applications, creating multiple paths into an account.

Anthropic’s operating model requires close connection between research values, product decisions, commercial growth, and real-world implementation. That makes deployment quality an extension of company credibility, not only a services
concern.

## Company Strategy & Operating Pressure
Anthropic’s safety-centered positioning creates a higher bar for how enterprise adoption is supported. Buyers and partners need practical guidance that connects model capability with security, governance, user change, and measurable value.

The company must balance reusable patterns with customer-specific needs. Too much standardization can limit relevance; too much customization can make ecosystem growth expensive, inconsistent, and difficult to govern.

A partnerships architecture function can help establish the middle ground: clear technical principles, reusable solution patterns, escalation paths, and disciplined feedback loops that improve both partner readiness and product
understanding.
